描述_EN: camels and horses were used as pack animals and merchants passed their goods from oasis to oasis. the victoria and albert museum has around 700 ancient and medieval textiles recovered by stein at the beginning of the twentieth century. this fragment was brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862–1943). the most notable item traded was silk. the site is part of an area now referred to as the silk road, a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia, from china to europe. the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas – while silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india in this way. it was recovered from the site of khadalik, a buddhist shrine dating from the 8th to the 10th century ad. some are silk while others are made from the wool of a variety of different animals. this circular mat is made up of a layer of cream felt in between two pieces of plain woven cream plant fibre bound with a strip of plain woven red plant fibre. the textiles range in date from the second century bc to the twelfth century ad.
描述_ZN: 年，骆驼和马被用作驮运动物，商人们在绿洲之间传递他们的货物。 年，维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆有大约700件古代和中世纪的纺织品，是斯坦在20世纪初找到的。 年，这块碎片由探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从中亚带回来。 年，最引人注目的贸易项目是丝绸。 年：该遗址是现在被称为 "丝绸之路 "的地区的一部分，这是一系列横跨亚洲、从中国到欧洲的陆上贸易路线。 年：丝绸之路对思想交流也很重要--当丝绸纺织品从中国向西运输时，佛教也通过这种方式从印度进入中国。 它是在Khadalik遗址中发现的，这是一个公元8-10世纪的佛教圣地。 有些是丝绸，有些则是由各种不同动物的羊毛制成。 这个圆形的垫子是由一层奶油色的毡子组成的，中间是两块平织的奶油色植物纤维，用一条平织的红色植物纤维捆绑。 这些纺织品的年代从公元前二世纪到公元十二世纪不等。
